utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, you have never earlier been to the village of Ljuboten either. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I understood it well, as you claim in your consolidated statement, this day you did not enter the village of Ljuboten either. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. The house was not inside the village of Ljuboten. It was outside of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this day you just came to the house where the video footage was recorded and you didn't go anywhere else from this house and then you returned to Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Ms. Cakar, that neither then on the 12th of August, when you were in the courtyard of this house, nor today you don't know whether this house is part or belongs to the village of Ljuboten or the village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This day when the editor-in-chief told you that have you to fulfil this task, you were the journalist on duty at the Macedonian TV and Radio. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, throughout the crisis in the Macedonian TV and Radio, duty teams have been organised, teams of journalists and cameramen who were working and on duty throughout the weekends as well. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. We had teams on duty during the weekend and during the weekdays in the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And these journalists and cameramen teams rotated and there was no strict rule which team and when will be working during the weekend. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The manner of work of each and every team would depend on the specific situation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, in the consolidated statement, in item 8 you said that in the initial information about Ljuboten you received on the 12th of August, 2001. Is this correct that you received this information only on Sunday, 12th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. And generally what was going on, this information I received by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although this was the 12th of August, at the moment when you received this task to go to the field, you didn't know at all what has happened on the 10th of August at Ljubotenski Bacila. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The only thing you knew about what was going on in the vicinity of Skopje was about the fights in Radusa because your colleague Sonja was reporting about these events. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I remembered, because I think this was an event that happened one day earlier, on Saturday. This is something that happened during my duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me if it is correct that your editor-in-chief gave this task to you after 1200 hours or if you can be more precise. Can you recall when your editor-in-chief gave you this task?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I cannot be very precise, but I'm rather sure that it wasn't before noon. It was after 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that this happened around -- or between 1200 and 1400 hours. Now you just told us that it was after 12.00. After giving your statement until the present day, when thinking about these events, were you able to remind yourself and remember about a more specific time when you were given this task?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I cannot be fully precise. However, if one takes into account that our duty shift would not start before 10.00 or 11.00 a.m., so I went to work, and this did not happen at the very same moment. So probably there was an hour or two between the moment when I came to work and when I got the task. And we did not depart immediately. I think that there were a couple of hours before we actually went to the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your editor-in-chief also told you that there will be an official vehicle coming to pick you up. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, as you have stated in your statement, you have reacted fiercefully regarding this task that you were given. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I have understood well, you said that the first reason for your reaction of this type was the fact that you were the only journalist on duty and you did not like to leave your duty at the Macedonian TV station, bearing in mind the possible news that might be received this particular day.

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. And because we have been working seven days a week, maybe more than ten hours a day, this was it. I was also tired, and I was on duty there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In several of the items in your statements, you say that you were afraid. The question is whether this fear about your personal safety, if you go to a particular region where there is danger, was this one of the reasons for your particular reaction for the task provided by your editor?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. As I already mentioned, I was tired, and every single time when we would have gone to the spot, this would mean that you can find yourself at a location where there -- where there might be some shooting, and this created pressure for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a journalist, did you have any kind of insurance at that time?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: There was no insurance of any kind, and we were not safe from any point of view, no equipment, no flakjackets or any greater experience or training how to behave in these kind of situations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, although you reacted in this manner, you had to accept and you did accept the task that was provided to you by your editor?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. Because at the end of the day, he had the final word, so it wasn't any issue of choice.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And following this overall conversation, you were picked up by an official vehicle, a regular official vehicle, and together with the cameraman you were taken to the building where the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia is located. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you waited there around 30 minutes, until the moment when the Minister Boskoski came out of the building and he joined you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: We were waiting for half an hour, maybe longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that it was obvious that you were scared, the minister offered to you to travel in the car that he would use, and the cameraman went to another car. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you have said that throughout the journey you were rather scared. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In item 13 of your consolidated statement, you claim that the minister along the road was trying to convince that there was nothing to be scared of. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was showing you the scenery, he was telling how wonderful is the nature in this area that you were travelling through. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Unlike me, the minister was behaving rather normally and not to use a wrong word but he was relaxed. He was acting normally and this is what we discussed. He was talking about the nature, how beautiful the nature in this particular region where we were at that particular moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And although you were afraid, you still managed to ask the minister what is the destination of your journey, but he did not respond to this kind of questions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I insisted all the way, all the time on information, Where are we going, why are we going there, what is going on from the very first moment, but I didn't receive any answer to these questions of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The minister did not answer this question but he continued to discuss the nature that you have been travelling through. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. Generally, he was talking about these kind of informal issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the manner in which he led the conversation and did not respond to your questions, can you tell me whether you have got the impression if the minister knew at all what was going on and where you were precisely headed to?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I don't know whether he knew, but maybe he didn't, because I didn't receive any kind of answer to my questions at any moment, direct or indirect; simply, the minister behaved as if he did not listen to my questions. He was continuing speaking on the topic that he has already started speaking on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And being a journalist, probably you had information that the minister quite often would have a very open conversations with the journalists?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: He was open to the journalists, and it was generally known that he wanted to be present in the media and he had regular contacts with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In item 14 of your consolidated statement, you say that you left from Skopje around 1400 hours. When we remind ourselves about the moment when you got your tasks and what you did at that moment when you left Skopje together with the minister, the question is whether this statement of yours is correct, that you did not leave from Skopje before 2.00 p.m. that day?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Not before 2.00, because I am sort of sure that we came back around 5.00, so when now going back, if we stayed there for an hour and a half, I don't know how long it takes to travel to -- to the spot. Maybe half an hour. So it is not possible for us to leave Skopje before 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that along the way you made a stop at a police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Neither you nor the minister left the vehicle at this particular moment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In item 15 of your consolidated statement, in relation to the question of the investigator, was it possible that a police vehicle was taking you from this police station, you answered that you do not exclude this possibility that you received a police escort from this police station. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Basically, I don't know but I do not exclude this as a possibility. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Before the house for which you later on found out that it is called Brace's house, you stopped at a police check-point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you mentioned in your statement, the minister shook hands at that place with the persons that were found there.

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. We stayed there just for a little while. There was some informal shaking of hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And those persons were wearing camouflage uniforms, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I don't know uniforms very much. I cannot make a distinction, but to me, camouflage means this multi-coloured uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know at all who these persons were that the minister shook hands with, whether they were members of the police or the army. You did not have any precise knowledge about who those persons were.

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the place where you briefly stayed, you heard strong gunshots which really increased your fear.

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. While we were at the check-point, at this moment, the shooting was louder or the strongest shooting during the period that I spent there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at that time you were not able to precisely conclude where does the fire come from, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When my learned colleague showed you the video, is it true that the first part of the recording showed part of the road in a sequence with the check-point where you stayed for a while?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I cannot remember with certainty now how were these sequences edited in the material, but I remember that part of the shots that we used for the material were shot at the check-point and that the other shots were shot in the yard of the house. No other recordings were made on other places.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The house you were standing in front of is somewhere between the check-point where you stayed briefly and the village of Ljuboten which is visible in the distance, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you mentioned that in your statement, and you said today -- oh, you didn't say it today. You said in your statement that you and the cameraman were running from the car to the yard while the minister walked normally, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Responding to my question earlier about the timing, you -- you had in mind the period that you stayed in a certain area and if I heard you well, you said that you spent around one to one and a half hour in the yard, right? Is that your response that you spent one and a half hour at the most in the yard?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I cannot be completely precise, but I think it was not longer than one and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if you say that you left Skopje by 2.00 at the latest, then you were not able at all to arrive in the yard of this house earlier than 2.30, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I'm not sure how long does it take from Skopje to that house, and how much time is needed to travel, but if you bear in mind that, I don't know, we stayed, like, five or ten minutes, we stopped at the police station on the way, so -- and we also spent some time at the check-point, so I assume that we had arrived at around 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your editor sent you for the assignment, and you were aware of that. You were aware of the fact that you should come with a certain information from that assignment, and that -- and that information would be published, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that was the reason you asked the minister in the yard of the Brace's house to give you a statement, but the minister refused to give any statements, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. I asked the minister for -- even when we arrived, I asked him to get a recorded statement, but the minister didn't give any statement, and at that point he didn't give any statement to me. But I needed that information in order to make my story, and I kept insisting to get a statement, to get at least some information, general information about what is going on, why we are here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And during the time you spoke with the minister and were asking for information, you were sitting at a stone chair with the minister inside the yard of this Brace house, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in that informal conversation, in that one and a half hour period while you stayed there, you received several of those information that you later transferred in your news that some action is in course, that the terrorists have entered the village, and the -- that some weapons have been seized and that a number of terrorists have been arrested. I very abbreviated this information, but my question is the following: Whether in that informal conversation that you have in the yard whereby you tried to find out some information, was that the manner in which you learned about those information at that time?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. Practically what I got was general information without any other details.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And bearing in mind what you already said about Minister Boskoski, did you think that the minister is hiding some information from you or that he sincerely said what he knew?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I did not insist to get other information after I asked questions, I was trying to get an answer, and after I got these answers, I don't know, I felt that that is it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The video that you were shown and that was shot by your cameraman, you recognised Minister Boskoski who was showing something with his hand in the air. Did you want to record the minister at that place?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Well, the minister was there, we were there, and since a TV crew is present at the field then, it is present there to register what is going on, and it was a normal thing if the minister was there to have him videotaped in that situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you said in your statement, the minister wanted to be recorded posing, not as really showing something to you, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Well, before starting to videotape, the cameraman asked him whether he could tape him, and the minister was aware that he is being taped. So at least from my position where I was, I didn't really see that something was happening outside of the fence. I didn't have an impression that, I don't know, there's something specific going on outside of the fence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 17 of your statement somewhere in the middle of it, you said that: "I had the impression that the minister wants to be videotaped as a hero. He was aware about the camera presence." Please tell me, is also today your feeling that he wanted to be seen by the camera as some kind of an important person there and that that wasn't any practical activity of the minister to really show you something or to really explain you something, but it was more of a pose, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I said previously that the minister wanted to be present in the media, bearing in mind that there was nothing going on, nothing special going on at that time there, nothing significant. I think that was more of a -- at that moment, that was more of a posing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Basically, from the place you were staying at you were not able to see anything, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: From the yard that we were in, it was very difficult to see the village or the houses in the village, and what was shown at the recording is practically that was just recorded by the camera. We were not able to see with the naked eye to see all this. We could just have a grasp of the houses, and we were able to see some smoke and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From that place, you were not able to see nor to follow any attack that was allegedly carried out by the police forces, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. We were not able to see anything else from there but some houses unclearly and some smoke from one or two places.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The minister, as well as you, was not able to see anything else, but you just said, some smoke and some houses?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Well, yes, bearing in mind that we were at the same place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but I was just going to say that the witness is being asked to speculate on what the minister actually saw. I don't believe she can speak to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness may be able to say what she could see standing by the minister, if we want to be very careful.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you were standing at the same places where the minister stood, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: At the -- not at the same moment when the cameraman was taping, but a few minutes before it and a few minutes after that, I was standing in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And from the -- from the place you were standing, you were not able to see anything else but what you just testified before this Court, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Especially, you weren't able to observe any police action that might have been taking place in Ljuboten, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. At that moment, nothing else was able to be seen, and nothing was happening in the field except for sporadic gunshots.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So during the time you spent in the Brace house, you already explained everything that you were able to see but you were able to see a weak sporadic fire, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that that fire was directed from the village towards the place where you were standing, would you agree with that or were you not able to assess where the sound of the sporadic fire was coming from?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I'm not able to assess.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Cakar, if someone were to testify before this Court the following: "[Previous translation continues] ... [In English] Known at the Chinese wall, Mr. Boskoski was able to view the ongoing attack by his police forces in Ljuboten," [Interpretation] Then you wouldn't be able to confirm it, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Please, could you say it once again? I lost it in the translation because I'm hearing both you and the interpreter at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "[In English] From behind a wall known as the Chinese wall, Mr. Boskoski was able to view the ongoing attack by his police forces in Ljuboten," [Interpretation] Then you wouldn't be able to agree with this statement, because something like that wasn't visible?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot agree, because something like that wasn't visible and couldn't be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to mention the page of the transcript just for the transcript. That is number 359. Your Honours, it might be a convenient time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We adjourn now, to resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, Ms. Cakar, the cameraman taped certain documents on this wooden -- of this stone table the identity cards and the passports which we were able to see in the recording that was shown?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were able to see that those were not documents issued by the Macedonian authorities, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. From what I was able to see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were told that those documents were seized from the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also in your statement you said that before leaving the garden, another group of persons entered the yard.

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your consolidated statement, in quotes, it has been put that those were the "special forces," and in your -- in the interview that you had with the Prosecutor once arriving in The Hague, you clarified that you have said that those are the so-called special forces because they were not wearing the regular police uniforms. Is that clarification of yours a clarification of that term special forces?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I would like to make it precise. In the statement when I came here in The Hague, it was written special forces. I wanted to clarify with the investigator and I insisted to leave that out because I never used that term, special forces. Because I already said previously I have no knowledge and I am not to be sure and decisive about what type of uniforms they were, whether those were the special force or not. I can only confirm that they were wearing uniforms. They were not wearing civilian clothes and that was it. And at that moment I wanted to clarify that. I never previously have said that those were the special forces from a simple reason that I don't know how the special forces look like.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the preparation for your testimony, you clearly said to the Prosecutor that you were sure that only those persons were not wearing the regular police uniforms, that is to say, the blue police uniforms, regularly worn by the police?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I only made it precise that I was aware that those were not the regular police uniforms as we can see the police officers wearing them on the streets.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not see any insignia or badges on the uniforms of those persons that entered the garden at that time, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I also said in my statement that I didn't notice any special insignia on the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in your statement you also said that the minister only casually said, How are you, something like that, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: That was when we were leaving, and there was no time for some, I don't know, some longer conversations. That was something informal, something like an informal brief conversation on passing by. It wasn't even a conversation like, How are you, how are you doing?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And for the entire time that you spent in the yard of the Brace house you never noticed the minister issuing orders to someone, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. There were no such situations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you bypassed that group that the minister just casually greeted with, How are you, you did not notice the minister calling by name any person or that the minister have recognised any of the persons, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: That lasted just briefly, without any formalities or personal -- or addressing personally someone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon, after your return to the radio and television house, you said you made a news report for the 5:00 newscasts, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. I reported via the telephone in the 5.00 newscast on my return, when returning on the way to Skopje, before we came to Skopje. That's how I was able to locate the time. I was called on the telephone to give a telephone report for the 5.00 news before we arrived in Skopje, but we have already departed from the house. So that was -- that took place sometime on the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you came, you started preparing the news segment from the task that you just completed, right?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, a complete news story with a video footage as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you said in paragraph 29 of your consolidated 92 ter statement, you said: [Previous translation continues] ... [In English] "Later showed this to my editor Dimovski that we only have a short scene with the minister. He was not satisfied with me. I first wrote the text for commenting the video and he read it. His comment was, Where is the minister here? I told him that we do have a part of the video showing the minister observing the situation. He told me to put this scene in." [Interpretation] Did it really happen in that way, that your editor asked you to put that shot of the minister in your story?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Actually, the editor expected to have more video footage that captured Minister Boskoski, but I just told him that we only had that shot where the minister is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And after that, you prepared an information in which you would show the minister and said that the minister is observing the situation. Is it correct that -- that also that approach of yours wasn't enough for the editor and that the editor requested that you write that the minister is heading the operation?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: The editor insisted to put wording whereby the role of the minister, role, the position of the minister will be maximally accentuated during that day. That wording was, I don't know, it wasn't enough strong for him. Although I insisted, I did not agree with him because from what we were able to observe in the field, practically that was -- that wording that the editor insisted on was not appropriate to what I saw in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This request of your editor, please tell me, did it originate partially from the editorial policy that was supposed to respond to the requirements of the times of crisis when certain energetic activities needed to be shown to the people, to the audience?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: There was a tendency to exaggerate certain issues, to show something in a more dramatic way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned to present in a dramatic way, did you understand in that way the comment of your editor also that he didn't like not seeing a lot of shooting in the -- in the videotaping, that the sounds of the battle are not heard very well?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: The first time the material was edited, these sounds were in the -- in the original, as recorded, but the editor insisted to have a better drama, bigger drama, to have larger parts of silence between the -- between the voiceover where we would be able hear more shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 31 of your consolidated statement, you said the following: "The editor ask me, Is there shooting, is it dramatically. I explained that at that time there was not a lot of shooting, then the editor insisted that I correct this." [Interpretation] Is this, in fact, the manner in which your editor asked for you to include this kind of dramatic events in your report?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you do so?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: The material was worked on again, and upon him insisting, we provided for more breaks between the text, the voiceover on the footage and the shooting sounds have been taken from the footage when we were at the check-point and not in the garden, because when we were staying at the check-point, the shooting was louder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this sound of the previous shootings that you could hear, you have repeated it on several occasions in order to show the situation as being more dramatic. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: The audio recording of the check-point basically is the audio presented in this material, and not the shooting, the sound from the period which we spent in the yard of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This means upon the request of your editor, you included in your report the wording that the minister managed the operation, although you were aware that this is not correct and that at any moment he did not manage with anything while he was staying in the Brace's house courtyard. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: It is a fact that when we were at this particular location up there I was not a witness of this type of situation. However, this was included in the narrative part of the report, upon the request from the editor. I reacted back then, I disagreed with this kind of approach. I insisted that we should be more precise, maybe at that moment this did not look so important to me. I could not even imagine that this kind of situation might appear, what is going on right now. But from my personal professional experience, generally speaking not for this case only, generally speaking, I think that this kind of approach in a certain situation even if a person believes it is justified, I think that in the future this can be quite counterproductive. And that is why even then I insisted that this should not be the case. I insisted for a more specific formulation and for things to be shown as they really happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you were not able to convince your editor and you had to act in accordance with his instructions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. There was an established hierarchy and, of course, his word was always the last one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The minister came with you and he left the Brace's house together with you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Accordingly, since you mentioned in your report, newscast that he managed the overall operation for the whole day, this would be also a rewarding presentation that would not correspond to the events that you witnessed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. This kind of formulation does not correspond to the events that I witnessed during these few hours in the courtyard of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just mentioned that you could not even imagine at that time that those additions and that dramatization of the situation could have had, as you said, these kind of consequences. Now I would like to ask you, Ms. Cakar, did you very soon in the media, in the public media, you heard that the Human Rights Watch organisation claims that Mr. Ljube Boskoski was in charge and he managed the operation in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I could see on the TV these kind of materials, and at that time there was a video footage presented from the report from the Macedonian TV and Radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown now Exhibit P352, page U000-0114, and this is the Human Rights Watch report dated 6th of the September, 2001. The e-court page is E000-114.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please take a look at the fourth paragraph of this report. It is in English, I will read it out and then you will receive the interpretation in Macedonian. And it reads: "[In English] The minister of the interior, Ljube Boskoski, was himself present in Ljuboten on Sunday, August 12th 2001, the day that the worst abuses documented in this report took place. The Macedonian national television, MTV, broadcasted that they, a copy of which was obtained by Human Rights Watch, shows Minister Boskoski on the balcony of an ethnic Macedonian's home on the northern outskirts of Ljuboten, surrounded by several armed policemen. According to the state television newscast, Minister Boskoski was present during the entire operation in the village." [Interpretation] On the top it reads 46, and in the bottom of the page it says this is a report of the Macedonian Television dated 12th of August, 2001. Is this something that you have understood quite soon, that this dramatically and incorrectly presented situation of Minister Boskoski is being used in order to point out towards his possibly -- possible responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Cakar, did anyone from Human Rights Watch or any other international organisation call you to ask you in what manner and how did you film and how did you produce and present this newscast?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone at any time from Human Rights Watch ask you whether all the facts that you have mentioned in your newscasts are correct or not?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will show you now one part of the statement by the witness Peter Bouckaert given before this Court. The question was -- this is page 2058 of the transcript and the line is from 1 to 7. 2958. "[Previous translation continues] ... [In English] We see on the left-hand side of this sketch, we see a road going up to the top of the page. We see a circle with an asterisk inside it and we see the words Boskoski house. What information were you recording there? "Answer: There was a house on the street which was pointed out to me as being the house where Mr. Boskoski had been present and had been filmed for national television during a part of the operation in Ljuboten." [Interpretation] As you can see, the witness Peter Bouckaert relies on the national TV station. Was this the report, the newscast that you produced, and the video footage that was filmed by your colleague, the cameraman this day?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: The video footage that was broadcasted, the only scene with the Minister Boskoski is the one where he stands in front of the fence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also on page 3074 of the transcript, Mr. Bouckaert was asked the following question: "[Previous translation continues] ... [In English] Under the subheading." [Interpretation] This is the part of the report of the Human Rights Watch that I have shown to you. [In English] "Responsibility of the security forces and the role of the Minister of the Interior Ljube Boskoski, do you see that? "Answer: Yes. "Question: And this section is essentially made of three photographs. Is that correct? "Answer: Yes. "Question: And the only reference, footnotes or authority given in the section is to MTV newscast on 12th of August, 2001. Is that correct? "Answer: That's correct. "Question: Is that also correct, Mr. Bouckaert, that you didn't seek to contact the television or the journalist which had prepared that broadcast? "Answer: That's correct." [Interpretation] Ms. Cakar, once again I am asking you, and this is something that Mr. Bouckaert confirmed in his statement. Peter Bouckaert nor anyone else from the Human Rights Watch organisation did not contact you in order to check the validity, the truthfulness of the information that was provided and presented in your newscast.

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. They never contacted me nor they spoke to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 3075, the question put to Mr. Bouckaert was the following [Previous translation continues] ... [In English] "You allege that Mr. Boskoski had been present during the entire operation. Is that correct? "Answer: No. We quote the state television newscast saying that Mr. Boskoski was present during the entire operation and we say later on that Mr. Boskoski has knowledge, that he was present at Ljuboten on Sunday, but maintained that he arrived around 4.00." [Interpretation] Ms. Cakar, you can now see that your information that the minister was present throughout the overall operation was taken over in the report presented by Human Rights Watch?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this the reason for which spontaneously earlier you mentioned that you were not able at that particular moment that this could have so far-reaching consequences?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: It is true that I could not guess that this can have such consequences but still I disagreed with this kind of approach. Even today I disagree. Even more now when I can see the consequences.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Cakar, do you believe that some people, especially people in those international organisations during the time of crisis, they were rather free taking over the -- taking the news from the Macedonian Television?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I would not like to be the judge of that, but I believe that they should have contacted me and to try and talk to me before releasing this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as one can see from the Human Rights Watch report, they immediately believed the information that was given in this newscast which was prepared in order to show the situation and the role of the Minister Boskoski in a dramatic way, which did not correspond with his true position that particular day. And I would like to ask you, since you mentioned it spontaneously yourself, are you aware that because of certain things that have not happened, then significant, very difficult consequences might have happened and indeed they did.

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I already mentioned at that particular moment I was not aware about a particular situation like this. But generally speaking, I was always aware that this kind of approach in the future can cause certain consequences or can have counter-effects. In this moment, I am also aware that this has happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how do you feel?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: In order not to feel sorry today, back then I reacted immediately, but now I'm sorry maybe for not being more persistent, although I doubt if I was able to change anything at that particular moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have any questions for this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I do have a few questions, if I can just have a moment to organise here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Cakar, in response to a question from my learned colleague earlier on, you answered that it was not -- you agreed with her that you were not able to conclude where firing was coming from while you were in the general Ljuboten area on the 12th of August, 2001. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you recall where smoke was coming from on that day?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: One or two locations one could see a smoke in the direction of the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And do you recall what was shown in the video-clip of people crouching behind a wall? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And where were they looking towards?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: The courtyard wall was in the direction towards the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So while gunshots were going off on that day, everyone's attention appeared to be directed towards Ljuboten. Would that be a fair comment?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: There was only a sporadic shooting that could be heard, and I'm not sure whether there was a lot of shooting at that moment. During this period, while we were in this courtyard, we could only hear weak sounds, sporadic fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. I do understand that. My question to you is, is it correct that everyone's attention appeared to be directed towards the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: When people were standing right next to the wall, they were looking towards the village, because the village was located at this side of the house. However, at that moment, as I already mentioned, there was nothing really special going on there. Almost nothing, with the exception of the smoke that we could see on one or two locations and just -- we could see the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And with regards to your answer which you also gave earlier on and you have repeated now that there was nothing special going on, there were gunshots weren't there, even if sporadic, there were gunshots, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, there were sporadic gunshots.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And there were -- you could see at least one or two houses that were on fire, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: One could see smoke. I think it was two locations where smoke could have been seen. But we were not able to see precisely whether it was a house burning from this particular location the visibility was not clear. However, we could see smoke coming from two locations, from the direction of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you also testified earlier on that you got a glimpse, even a fleeting glimpse of some people were being detained during the operation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: I will repeat. I was running and I was aware about the presence of people to my left side, but I did not turn and I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I just want to get clear on this. You testified that you didn't believe there was anything special going on, but you were aware that there were gunshots, there were houses on fire, and that there were people who you understood had been seized in this operation. Is my understanding correct here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to this line of questioning, because the witness never mentioned that there were houses burning in the village nor did she say that she knew there were houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I can rephrase that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, go ahead. I would have thought, though, that if the video film that was taken as she was there looking indicated the scene in front of her, knowledge of fire was inevitable, but Mr. Dobbyn will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So my question to you is that, in light of your statement that there was nothing special going on you were aware, weren't you, that there were gunshots, you were aware that there was smoke coming from the village, and you were aware that there -- there were people who had been seized in the operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELI CAKAR
utterances.text: That there are people arrested, I didn't see that. This is something I received as an information, that during the action people have been arrested who will be taken to a police station later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, you've also testified in response to some questions that -- actually, Your Honours, is this a good time to break or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we do have another trial continuing at 2.15, so we must now adjourn and we will need to continue your evidence tomorrow morning at 9.00. So we must now adjourn with a view to continuing tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
